<hypothesis>
kind: hypothesis
title: Target-Model-Guided Prompt Compression via Attention Saliency
hypothesis: >-
  Using the target LLM's own attention-saliency maps or gradient-based input attribution (e.g., integrated gradients, attention
  rollout) to select which prompt tokens to retain will outperform proxy-model-based compression (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua,
  LLMLingua-2) because it directly captures what the target model actually uses for generation, rather than what a small proxy
  model thinks is important.
motivation: >-
  All existing prompt compression methods (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2, Selective-Context, PCRL, Perception Compressor)
  use a SMALL PROXY MODEL (GPT-2, LLaMA-7B, BERT, etc.) to estimate token importance. This creates a distribution mismatch:
  the proxy model's notion of 'important tokens' may not match what the actual target LLM attends to during generation. By
  using the target model's own attention or gradient-based saliency, we directly measure what the target model uses, eliminating
  the proxy gap. This is especially impactful for open models (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen) where we have full white-box access to
  attention maps.
assumptions:
- >-
  The target LLM's attention patterns or input gradients correlate with token importance for the downstream task
- >-
  White-box access to the target model is available (open-weight models like LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen)
- >-
  Attention-saliency can be computed efficiently (single forward pass or few backward passes) relative to the compression
  budget
- >-
  The target model's attention on the prompt tokens is stable across similar prompts/tasks (enabling caching or reuse)
investigation_approach: >-
  Implement a tiny experiment comparing three compression strategies on LongBench (single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization)
  using LLaMA-3-8B as the target model: (1) LLMLingua (GPT-2 perplexity baseline), (2) LongLLMLingua (query-aware contrastive
  perplexity), (3) Target-Model-Guided: compute attention rollout or integrated gradients from the target model on a calibration
  set, use mean attention-to-prompt or gradient magnitude per token as importance score, compress by retaining top-k tokens.
  Measure F1/ROUGE vs compression ratio. Total compute: <1 GPU-hour on a single A100/H100.
success_criteria: >-
  Target-model-guided compression achieves higher task performance (F1 for QA, ROUGE for summarization) than LLMLingua and
  LongLLMLingua at the same compression ratios (2x, 4x, 8x) on at least 2 of 3 LongBench task categories. A null result (no
  improvement) would still be informative—it would suggest the proxy models already capture the target model's token importance
  well, or that attention-saliency is not the right signal.
related_works:
- >-
  LLMLingua (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023): Uses GPT-2/LLaMA-7B perplexity as proxy for token importance. Fundamentally differs
  by using a small proxy model instead of the target model's own attention.
- >-
  LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al., ACL 2024): Adds query-awareness via contrastive perplexity (perplexity shift when conditioned
  on question). Still uses a proxy model (LLaMA-7B) for all importance estimates.
- >-
  LLMLingua-2 (Pan et al., ACL Findings 2024): Trains a BERT-based token classifier on GPT-4 distilled data. Task-agnostic,
  uses bidirectional context but still a proxy model (XLM-RoBERTa/mBERT), not the target LLM.
- >-
  Selective-Context (Li et al., 2023): Uses self-information from a small LM. Proxy-based, no query awareness.
- >-
  PCRL (Jung & Kim, 2023): RL-based discrete compression with ROUGE reward. Trains a policy on a small model (DistilBERT),
  not the target LLM.
- >-
  Perception Compressor (Tang et al., NAACL 2025): Training-free, uses guiding questions and contrast perplexity from a small
  LM. Still proxy-based.
- >-
  Attention-based KV cache compression (e.g., Keyformer, PyramidInfer): Uses target model attention to drop KV cache entries
  DURING generation, not for prompt compression BEFORE generation. Different problem setting.
inspiration: >-
  Cross-domain transfer from mechanistic interpretability (attribution patching, activation patching) and model compression
  (attention-guided pruning). In mechanistic interpretability, we routinely use the target model's own attention/activations
  to understand its behavior. In model compression (e.g., MiniLMv2, attention distillation), we use teacher model attention
  to guide student training. The novel move is applying target-model attention/attribution to PROMPT COMPRESSION (selecting
  input tokens) rather than model compression (selecting weights/heads) or KV cache compression (selecting past keys/values).
  This connects the interpretability insight 'the model tells you what it attends to' with the prompt compression problem
  'which input tokens matter'.
terms:
- term: Proxy model
  definition: >-
    A smaller, faster model (e.g., GPT-2, LLaMA-7B, BERT) used to estimate token importance for compressing prompts intended
    for a larger target LLM
- term: Target model
  definition: >-
    The actual LLM that will process the compressed prompt at inference time (e.g., LLaMA-3-8B, Mistral-7B, GPT-4)
- term: Attention rollout
  definition: >-
    A method to compute token-to-token attribution by recursively multiplying attention matrices across layers, showing how
    much each input token contributes to each output token
- term: Integrated gradients
  definition: >-
    A gradient-based attribution method that integrates gradients along a straight-line path from a baseline input to the
    actual input, providing token-level importance scores
- term: Attention-saliency map
  definition: >-
    A per-token importance score derived from the target model's attention patterns, e.g., mean attention received by each
    prompt token across heads and layers
- term: Contrastive perplexity
  definition: >-
    LongLLMLingua's metric: perplexity(token | context) - perplexity(token | question, context), measuring how much the question
    reduces uncertainty about a token
summary: >-
  Current prompt compression methods all rely on small proxy models to decide which tokens to keep. This hypothesis proposes
  using the target LLM's own attention-saliency or gradient-based input attribution directly—measuring what the target model
  actually attends to—eliminating the proxy gap. Tiny experiments on LongBench with LLaMA-3-8B can validate this in <1 GPU-hour.
alternates:
- title: Calibration-Set Attention Distillation
  hypothesis: >-
    Instead of computing attention per-query, pre-compute a universal token-importance profile for the target model on a small
    calibration set (e.g., 100 diverse prompts), then use this static profile for all future compressions. This amortizes
    the white-box cost and tests whether the target model has consistent attention patterns across tasks.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    If the target model's attention-to-prompt-tokens is relatively stable across tasks (e.g., always attends to instructions,
    entity names, question words), a one-time calibration suffices. This would be dramatically faster than per-query attribution
    and more practical for production. It beats the main hypothesis if per-query computation is the bottleneck and attention
    patterns are task-invariant.
- title: Hybrid Proxy-Target Compression
  hypothesis: >-
    Use the proxy model (e.g., LLMLingua-2) for coarse-grained document/sentence selection (cheap, fast), then apply target-model
    attention-saliency only for fine-grained token selection within the retained segments. This combines the efficiency of
    proxy models with the accuracy of target-model guidance.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    Pure target-model attribution on 10k-token prompts may be slow. Coarse proxy filtering reduces the token budget for expensive
    target-model attribution. This beats the main hypothesis if the compute budget is tight and coarse proxy decisions are
    already near-optimal, leaving only fine-grained selection to benefit from target-model signals.
- title: Gradient-Free Attention Sinks for Black-Box Target Models
  hypothesis: >-
    For API-only target models (no white-box access), use the 'attention sink' phenomenon (first few tokens accumulate disproportionate
    attention) as a proxy for the target model's internal attention: retain tokens that would become attention sinks (early
    instruction tokens, question tokens) and use a small proxy model for the rest.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    The main hypothesis requires white-box access. If the attention sink pattern is universal and predictable, we can approximate
    target-model attention without access. This beats the main hypothesis in black-box settings (OpenAI API, Anthropic API)
    where the main hypothesis is inapplicable. It wins if attention sinks reliably indicate target-model importance across
    diverse prompts.
_relation_rationale: >-
  Same conceptual frame; defects in experimental pipeline prevent any evidence from bearing on the claim.

     9	  "answer": "This research surveys three recent prompt compression methods and proposes one small novel variant for tiny experiments on LongBench with LLaMA-3-8B.\n\n1) LLMLingua-2 (Wang et al., 2024): Replaces iterative perplexity dropping with a BERT-based token classifier. The public model is available on Hugging Face under identifiers such as microsoft/llmlingua-2-bert-base. Inference uses standard transformers AutoTokenizer and a sequence-classification model to score token keep probabilities. API differences from v1 include the absence of iterative proxy forward passes and faster segment-level batching. Key hyperparameters: token-score threshold around 0.5-0.7 and segment lengths of 64-256 tokens. This method is the fastest among the three because it avoids per-prompt proxy perplexity computation [1, 4].\n\n2) LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al., 2024): Extends LLMLingua with question-aware contrastive perplexity, comparing p(token|context) and p(token|question+context) to bias retention toward query-relevant tokens. It remains in the llmlingua repository. Key API difference from v1 is the use_question_as_condition flag and document-level scoring. Computational cost is higher than v1 because it computes conditional probabilities for both question-free and question-conditioned contexts. Code usage passes the question and context through the compressor and selects documents or tokens with higher contrastive importance [2, 4].\n\n3) Selective Context (Li et al., 2023): Uses an information-theoretic criterion to filter tokens based on self-information or redundancy measured by a small language model. It removes tokens that are predictable given surrounding context, using a sliding-window perplexity estimator. API is lightweight: load a small GPT-2 or LLaMA-7B tokenizer and model, compute token-level negative log-likelihood, and drop high-probability tokens subject to a minimum token budget. Key hyperparameters: window size, stride, and minimum token budget. It is simple to implement and computationally cheap, but may drop fewer tokens than LLMLingua-2 at the same compression ratio [14, 15].\n\n4) Proposed small novel variant: Calibrated Attention Dropout Compression (CADC). CADC trains a lightweight calibration layer offline by averaging attention-flow or integrated-gradient scores over a small calibration set, then uses this static profile to guide proxy-based token dropping at inference. Specifically, it combines LLMLingua-2 token scores with cached target-model attention priors via a weighted sum, thresholds the combined score, and drops tokens. The variant is small because it avoids per-request target-model attribution and keeps runtime near LLMLingua-2. It is novel in conditioning proxy dropout on offline target-model attention priors, which prior work leaves unused. For tiny experiments, use 20-100 calibration prompts, prior weight 0.1-0.3, and compression ratios 2x/4x/8x on one LongBench task subset [9, 10].\n\nImplementation code patterns are provided in recipe_card.md.      1	# Recipe Card: Prompt Compression with Target-Model Attribution

     7	from llmlingua import PromptCompressor
     8	compressor = PromptCompressor(device_map="auto")
     9	compressed = compressor.compress_prompt(
    10	    prompt,

    21	
    22	### 2. LongLLMLingua

    24	compressed = compressor.compress_prompt(
    25	    prompt,

    28	    target_token=256,
    29	    compression_ratio=0.5,
    30	    use_question_as_condition=True
    31	)
    32	```
    33	Notes: Contrastive perplexity compares `p(token|context)` and `p(token|question+context)`.
    34	
    35	### 3. LLMLingua-2
    36	```python
    37	from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
    38	model_name = "microsoft/llmlingua-2-bert-base"
    39	tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    40	model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name)
    41	inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
    42	logits = model(**inputs).logits
    43	scores = logits.softmax(-1)[..., 1]  # keep probability
    44	mask = scores > 0.5
    45	compressed_ids = inputs.input_ids[mask]
    46	compressed = tokenizer.decode(compressed_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
    47	```
    48	Notes: BERT classifier predicts token-level importance. API differs from v1 by avoiding iterative forward passes.
    49	
    50	### 4. Attention rollout
    51	```python
    52	def attention_rollout(attentions, residual=True):
    53	    # attentions: list of (batch, heads, seq, seq)
    54	    rollout = torch.eye(attentions[0].shape[-1]).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
    55	    rollout = rollout.to(attentions[0].device)
    56	    for att in attentions:
    57	        att = att.mean(dim=1)  # mean over heads
    58	        if residual:
    59	            att = att + torch.eye(att.shape[-1]).to(att.device)
    60	        rollout = torch.matmul(rollout, att)
    61	        rollout = rollout / (rollout.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
    62	    return rollout.squeeze(0).squeeze(0)  # token importance
    63	```
    64	Notes: Requires `output_attentions=True`. Memory heavy on long contexts.
    65	
    66	### 5. Integrated gradients
    67	```python
    68	from captum.attr import LayerIntegratedGradients
    69	lig = LayerIntegratedGradients(model, model.bert.embeddings)
    70	attributions = lig.attribute(
    71	    inputs=inputs.input_ids,
    72	    baselines=torch.zeros_like(inputs.input_ids),
    73	    target=0,
    74	    n_steps=50
    75	)
    76	scores = attributions.sum(dim=-1)
    77	```
    78	Notes: Baseline can be zero embeddings or padding embeddings. Use 20-50 steps.
    79	
    80	### 6. Hybrid proxy-target compression
    81	```python
    82	# Stage 1: proxy selection
    83	proxy_ids = proxy_model.select_sentences(prompt, budget=0.5)
    84	# Stage 2: target attribution
    85	target_ids = target_model.attribute_tokens(proxy_ids)
    86	mask = target_ids > threshold
    87	compressed_ids = proxy_ids[mask]
    88	```
    89	Notes: Reduces cost by compressing before expensive attribution.
    90	
    91	### 7. Attention sinks fallback
    92	```python
    93	sink_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids, dtype=torch.bool)
    94	sink_mask[:N] = True  # retain first N tokens
    95	sink_mask[question_mask] = True  # retain query tokens
    96	mask = sink_mask | attribution_mask
    97	compressed_ids = inputs_ids[mask]
    98	```
    99	Notes: Cheap black-box approximation; strongest in streaming-trained models.
   100	
   101	### 8. CADC variant
   102	```python
   103	# Offline calibration
   104	cal_scores = []
   105	for prompt in calibration_set:
   106	    s = target_model.attention_rollout(prompt)
   107	    cal_scores.append(s)
   108	prior = torch.stack(cal_scores).mean(0)
   109	
   110	# Online compression
   111	attrib = proxy_model.classify(prompt)
   112	combined = attrib + prior_weight * prior
   113	mask = combined > threshold
   114	compressed = decode(mask)
   115	```
   116	Notes: Keeps runtime near LLMLingua-2 by caching attention priors.

   131	- Benchmark: LongBench [12, 13].

   133	- Compression ratios: 2x, 4x, 8x.

   141	## D. Compute requirements
   142	- Proxy methods: CPU acceptable for 10k tokens; small model forward passes dominate.
   143	- Attention rollout and integrated gradients: GPU recommended; 10k tokens may require chunking.
   144	- LLMLingua-2: Fastest; suitable for CPU/GPU batching.
   145	- Hybrid: Reduces target attribution cost by reducing token count first.

   104	
   105	## Phase 3: Attention Rollout Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   106	
   107	### 3.1 Method Description
   108	The attention rollout method computes token importance by multiplying attention matrices across all transformer layers. This captures higher-order token interactions.
   109	
   110	**Algorithm:**
   111	1. For each layer `i`, extract attention matrix `A_i ∈ R^(L×L)`
   112	2. Add identity matrix: `A_i' = A_i + I` (residual connections)
   113	3. Rollout product: `A_final = A_1' × A_2' × ... × A_N'`
   114	4. Normalize: `S = A_final / sum(A_final)`
   115	5. Token importance = row sums of `S`
   116	
   117	### 3.2 Implementation Code
   118	```python
   119	import torch
   120	import numpy as np
   121	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   122	
   123	class AttentionRollout:
   124	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   125	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   126	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   127	        self.device = device
   128	        self.attention_matrices = []
   129	        
   130	    def extract_attention(self, layer_id, attention, tokens):
   131	        """Extract attention matrix from a transformer layer."""
   132	        # attention shape: (batch, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
   133	        # Average across heads
   134	        attn = attention[0].mean(dim=1)  # (seq_len, seq_len)
   135	        self.attention_matrices.append(attn.detach().cpu().numpy())
   136	    
   137	    def compute_rollout(self, text):
   138	        """Compute attention rollout token importance scores."""
   139	        tokens = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   140	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   141	        
   142	        self.attention_matrices = []
   143	        
   144	        # Register hook to extract attention from each layer
   145	        hooks = []
   146	        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model.encoder.layer):
   147	            hook = layer.attention.register_forward_hook(
   148	                lambda layer_id=i, attention=None: 
   149	                    self.extract_attention(layer_id, attention, tokens)
   150	            )
   151	            hooks.append(hook)
   152	        
   153	        # Forward pass
   154	        with torch.no_grad():
   155	            output = self.model(**tokens)
   156	        
   157	        # Remove hooks
   158	        for hook in hooks:
   159	            hook.remove()
   160	        
   161	        # Compute rollout product
   162	        A_final = np.eye(len(tokens["input_ids"][0]))
   163	        for A_i in self.attention_matrices:
   164	            A_i = A_i + np.eye(A_i.shape[0])  # Add identity
   165	            A_final = A_final @ A_i
   166	        
   167	        # Normalize and compute importance
   168	        row_sums = A_final.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
   169	        S = A_final / row_sums
   170	        importance = S.sum(axis=1)  # Row sums = token importance
   171	        
   172	        return importance, tokens
   173	```
   174	
   175	### 3.3 Expected Output
   176	- Token importance scores for each position in the input
   177	- Higher scores indicate more important tokens
   178	- Can be used to rank and prune tokens
   179	
   180	---
   181	
   182	## Phase 4: Integrated Gradients Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   183	
   184	### 4.1 Method Description
   185	Integrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the input. For LLMs, this attributes importance to each token based on how much it contributes to the output.
   186	
   187	**Algorithm:**
   188	1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or `<PAD>` token)
   189	2. Create interpolation: `x'(α) = baseline + α × (input - baseline)` for `α ∈ [0,1]`
   190	3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point
   191	4. Integrate: `IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) × ∫₀¹ (∂F/∂x_i)(x'(α)) dα`
   192	5. Sum across layers for final attribution
   193	
   194	### 4.2 Implementation Code
   195	```python
   196	import torch
   197	from captum.attr import IntegratedGradients
   198	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   199	
   200	class IntegratedGradientsAttribution:
   201	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   202	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   203	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   204	        self.device = device
   205	        
   206	    def compute_ig(self, text, baseline_text="[PAD]", target_layer=-1):
   207	        """Compute integrated gradients token attributions."""
   208	        # Tokenize input and baseline
   209	        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   210	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   211	        baselines = self.tokenizer(baseline_text, return_tensors="pt", 
   212	                                   max_length=512).to(self.device)
   213	        
   214	        # Pad baseline to same length as input
   215	        b_input_ids = baselines["input_ids"].repeat(1, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1])
   216	        b_attention_mask = baselines["attention_mask"].repeat(1, inputs["attention_mask"].shape[1])
   217	        
   218	        # Initialize IG
   219	        ig = IntegratedGradients(self.model)
   220	        
   221	        # Compute attributions
   222	        attributions = ig.attribute(
   223	            inputs={"input_ids": b_input_ids, "attention_mask": b_attention_mask},
   224	            target=target_layer,
   225	            n_steps=50,  # Number of interpolation steps
   226	            internal_batch_size=8
   227	        )
   228	        
   229	        # Extract toke<response clipped><NOTE>Due to the max output limit, only part of this file has been shown to you. You should retry this tool after you have searched inside the file with `grep -n` in order to find the line numbers of what you are looking for.</NOTE># 8.1 Evaluation Metrics

   277	### 8.3 LongBench Evaluation Protocol
   278	```python
   279	def evaluate_on_longbench(method, dataset, model, tokenizer):
   280	    """Evaluate a method on LongBench benchmark."""
   281	    results = {}
   282	    
   283	    for task_type in ["niah", "multidoc_qa", "single_qa", "summary", "code", "knowledge"]:
   284	        task_data = dataset[task_type]
   285	        task_results = []
   286	        
   287	        for example in task_data:
   288	            context = example["context"]
   289	            question = example["question"]
   290	            expected_answer = example["answer"]
   291	            
   292	            # Compress context using the method
   293	            compressed_context = method.compress(context)
   294	            
   295	            # Run model with compressed input
   296	            full_input = f"{compressed_context}\nQuestion: {question}"
   297	            response = model.generate(full_input)
   298	            
   299	            # Evaluate
   300	            score = compute_score(response, expected_answer, task_type)
   301	            task_results.append(score)
   302	        
   303	        results[task_type] = {
   304	            "mean_score": np.mean(task_results),
   305	            "std_score": np.std(task_results),
   306	            "num_examples": len(task_results)
   307	        }
   308	    
   309	    return results
   310	```

   317	```python
   318	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
   319	import seaborn as sns
   320	import numpy as np
   321	
   322	def plot_token_importance_comparison(results, tokenizer, title="Token Importance Comparison"):
   323	    """Plot token importance scores from different methods."""
   324	    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(results), 1, figsize=(12, 3*len(results)))
   325	    
   326	    for i, (method_name, data) in enumerate(results.items()):
   327	        if isinstance(data, dict) and "scores" in data:

   329	        else:

   334	        axes[i].set_title(method_name)
   335	        axes[i].set_xlabel("Token Position")
   336	        axes[i].set_ylabel("Importance Score")
   337	    
   338	    plt.tight_layout()
   339	    plt.savefig("token_importance_comparison.png", dpi=150)

   341	
   342	def plot_correlation_heatmap(results):
   343	    """Plot correlation between methods' importance scores."""
   344	    method_names = list(results.keys())
   345	    n_methods = len(method_names)
   346	    corr_matrix = np.zeros((n_methods, n_methods))
   347	    
   348	    for i, m1 in enumerate(method_names):
   349	        for j, m2 in enumerate(method_names):
   350	            s1 = results[m1]["scores"] if "scores" in results[m1] else results[m1]
   351	            s2 = results[m2]["scores"] if "scores" in results[m2] else results[m2]
   352	            corr_matrix[i, j] = np.corrcoef(s1, s2)[0, 1]
   353	    
   354	    sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, xticklabels=method_names, 
   355	                yticklabels=method_names, cmap="RdBu_r")
   356	    plt.title("Correlation Between Token Importance Methods")
   357	    plt.savefig("importance_correlation.png", dpi=150)
   358	```

   360	### 9.2 Key Analysis Questions
   361	1. **Correlation Analysis**: How correlated are attention rollout and integrated gradients scores?
   362	2. **Compression Quality**: Which method preserves task accuracy best at 50% compression?
   363	3. **Long-context Behavior**: How do methods differ on 10k+ token inputs?
   364	4. **Speed-Quality Tradeoff**: What is the inference speedup vs quality loss for each method?
   365	5. **Token Type Sensitivity**: Do methods agree on which punctuation/content words to remove?

   394	
   395	| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
   396	|------|--------|------------|
   397	| Out of memory on long contexts | High | Use sliding window, gradient checkpointing, smaller models |
   398	| Slow inference on large models | Medium | Use smaller models for testing, batch processing |
   399	| Inconsistent results across methods | Medium | Use multiple seeds, multiple prompts |
   400	| Captum compatibility issues | Low | Use alternative SHAP library, manual IG implementation |

   115	def token_f1(pred: str, gold: str) -> float:
   116	    """Compute token-level F1 score."""
   117	    pred_tokens = pred.lower().split()
   118	    gold_tokens = gold.lower().split()
   119	    if not pred_tokens or not gold_tokens:
   120	        return 0.0
   121	    pred_set = defaultdict(int)
   122	    gold_set = defaultdict(int)
   123	    for t in pred_tokens:
   124	        pred_set[t] += 1
   125	    for t in gold_tokens:
   126	        gold_set[t] += 1
   127	    common = sum(min(pred_set[k], gold_set[k]) for k in pred_set)
   128	    if common == 0:
   129	        return 0.0
   130	    precision = common / len(pred_tokens)
   131	    recall = common / len(gold_tokens)
   132	    return 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0.0

   285	    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer):
   286	        self.name = "longllmlingua"
   287	        self.model = model

   291	    def _compute_perplexity(self, text: str) -> float:
   292	        """Compute perplexity of text using the model."""
   293	        try:
   294	            enc = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=1024)
   295	            with torch.no_grad():
   296	                outputs = self.model(**enc.to(self.model.device))
   297	                logits = outputs.logits
   298	                loss_fct = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")
   299	                shift_logits = logits[..., :-1, :].contiguous()
   300	                shift_labels = enc["input_ids"][..., 1:].contiguous()
   301	                loss = loss_fct(shift_logits.view(-1, shift_logits.size(-1)), shift_labels.view(-1))
   302	                return torch.exp(loss.mean()).item()
   303	        except Exception:
   304	            return float("inf")
   305	
   306	    def _token_perplexity(self, text: str, token_pos: int) -> float:
   307	        """Compute perplexity contribution of a single token."""
   308	        tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
   309	        if token_pos >= len(tokens):
   310	            return 0.0
   311	        prefix = self.tokenizer.decode(tokens[:token_pos + 1])
   312	        suffix = self.tokenizer.decode(tokens[token_pos:token_pos + 1])
   313	        perp_full = self._compute_perplexity(prefix + suffix)
   314	        perp_without = self._compute_perplexity(prefix)
   315	        return max(0.0, perp_full - perp_without)

   319	        try:

   324	            # Compute importance scores for each token

   329	                scores.append(s)
   330	                if i % 20 == 0:

   333	            scores = np.array(scores)

   336	            keep_indices = sorted(keep_indices)

   338	            kept_tokens = [tokens[i] for i in keep_indices]

   344	                "original_len": len(tokens),
   345	                "compressed_len": num_keep
   346	            }
   347	        except Exception as e:

   439	class AttentionRolloutMethod:
   440	    """M4: Target-Attention - Uses attention rollout from the target model to score tokens."""
   441	
   442	    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer):
   443	        self.name = "attention_rollout"
   444	        self.model = model
   445	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
   446	        self.attention_matrices = []
   447	        self._hooks_registered = False
   448	        self.available = True
   449	
   450	    def _register_hooks(self):
   451	        """Register hooks to capture attention matrices from each layer."""
   452	        self.attention_matrices = []
   453	        self.hooks = []
   454	
   455	        def make_hook(layer_idx):
   456	            def hook(module, input, output):
   457	                # output is tuple, first element is attention output
   458	                if hasattr(module, 'attn') and module.attn is not None:
   459	                    attn = module.attn
   460	                elif hasattr(module, 'self_attn'):
   461	                    attn = module.self_attn
   462	                else:
   463	                    return
   464	                # Get attention weights (from the attention module)
   465	                try:
   466	                    if hasattr(attn, 'weight'):
   467	                        self.attention_matrices.append(attn.weight.detach().cpu())
   468	                    elif hasattr(module, 'out_proj'):
   469	                        self.attention_matrices.append(module.out_proj.weight.detach().cpu())
   470	                except Exception:
   471	                    pass
   472	            return hook
   473	
   474	        # Try to register hooks on attention layers
   475	        try:
   476	            for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
   477	                if "attention" in name.lower() or "self_attn" in name.lower():
   478	                    hook = module.register_forward_hook(make_hook(name))
   479	                    self.hooks.append(hook)
   480	            self._hooks_registered = True
   481	            logger.info(f"Registered {len(self.hooks)} attention hooks")
   482	        except Exception as e:

   484	            self.available = False

   486	    def _compute_attention_rollout(self, text: str) -> np.ndarray:
   487	        """Compute attention rollout scores for each token."""
   488	        try:
   489	            enc = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)

   498

   501	                return np.ones(input_ids.shape[1])

   514	            importance = rollout.sum(dim=-1).cpu().numpy()

   675	                "compressed_len": num_keep
   676	            }
   677	        except Exception as e:
   678	            logger.error(f"Calibration compression failed: {e}")
   679	            return text, {"error": str(e)}
   680	
   681	    def __repr__(self):
   682	        return f"CalibrationDistilled(static_profile_from_{NUM_CALIBRATION_PROMPTS}_prompts)"
   683	
   684	
   685	# ─── Method 6: Hybrid (LLMLingua-2 Coarse + Target-Attention Fine) ────────────
   686	
   687	class HybridMethod:
   688	    """M6: Hybrid - LLMLingua-2 coarse filter + Target-Attention fine selection."""
   689	
   690	    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer):
   691	        self.name = "hybrid"
   692	        self.model = model
   693	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
   694	        self.llmlingua2 = LLMLingua2Method(model, tokenizer)
   695	        self.attention = AttentionRolloutMethod(model, tokenizer)
   696	        self.available = True
   697	
   698	    def compress(self, text: str, rate: float) -> tuple[str, dict]:
   699	        """Compress using hybrid approach."""
   700	        try:
   701	            tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
   702	            if len(tokens) < 2:
   703	                return text, {"error": "too short"}
   704	
   705	            # Step 1: LLMLingua-2 to 50% (coarse filter)
   706	            intermediate_text, llmlingua2_info = self.llmlingua2.compress(text, rate=2.0)
   707	            intermediate_tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(intermediate_text, add_special_tokens=False)
   708	
   709	            # Step 2: On retained tokens, compute attention rollout
   710	            if len(intermediate_tokens) < 2:
   711	                # Fallback to just LLMLingua-2
   712	                return intermediate_text, {"method": "hybrid", "llmlingua2_info": llmlingua2_info}
   713	
   714	            intermediate_text_full = self.tokenizer.decode(intermediate_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
   715	            attn_info = self.attention._compute_attention_rollout(intermediate_text_full)
   716	
   717	            # Combine: keep top-k from attention-scored intermediate tokens
   718	            n_tokens = len(intermediate_tokens)
   719	            num_keep = max(1, int(n_tokens / rate))
   720	            importance = attn_info[:n_tokens] if len(attn_info) >= n_tokens else np.ones(n_tokens)
   721	            keep_indices = np.argsort(importance)[-num_keep:]
   722	            keep_indices = sorted(keep_indices)
   723	
   724	            kept_tokens = [intermediate_tokens[i] for i in keep_indices]
   725	            compressed_text = self.tokenizer.decode(kept_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
   726	
   727	            return compressed_text, {
   728	                "method": "hybrid",
   729	                "llmlingua2_tokens": len(intermediate_tokens),
   730	                "final_tokens": num_keep,
   731	                "original_len": len(tokens),
   732	                "compressed_len": num_keep
   733	            }
   734	        except Exception as e:
   735	            logger.error(f"Hybrid compression failed: {e}")
   736	            return text, {"error": str(e)}
   737	
   738	    def __repr__(self):
   739	        return f"Hybrid(LLMLingua2_coarse+Attention_fine)"
   740	
   741	
   742	# ─── Method 7: Attention-Sink (First-k + Proxy) ──────────────────────────────
   743	
   744	class AttentionSinkMethod:
   745	    """M7: Attention-Sink - First-k tokens (bos, instruction, question) + proxy-selected tokens."""
   746	
   747	    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer):
   748	        self.name = "attention_sink"
   749	        self.model = model
   750	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
   751	        self.proxy = LLMLinguaMethod(model, tokenizer)
   752	        self.k = 3  # attention sink count
   753	        self.available = True
   754	
   755	    def compress(self, text: str, rate: float) -> tuple[str, dict]:
   756	        """Compress using attention-sink approach."""
   757	        try:
   758	            tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
   759	            if len(tokens) < 2:
   760	                return text, {"error": "too short"}
   761	
   762	            # Compute sink count: max(3, int(total_tokens * 0.1))
   763	            k = max(self.k, int(len(tokens) * 0.1))
   764	            k = min(k, len(tokens) - 1)
   765	
   766	            # Use proxy to score remaining tokens (after first k)
   767	            remaining_tokens = tokens[k:]
   768	            remaining_text = self.tokenizer.decode(remaining_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
   769	            proxy_result = self.proxy.compress(remaining_text, rate=rate)
   770	
   771	            if "error" in proxy_result[1]:
   772	                # Fallback: just keep first k + random
   773	                num_keep = max(k, int(len(tokens) / rate))
   774	                keep_indices = list(range(min(k, len(tokens))))
   775	                extra_needed = num_keep - k
   776	                if extra_needed > 0:
   777	                    keep_indices.extend(np.random.choice(
   778	                        range(k, len(tokens)), size=min(extra_needed, len(tokens) - k), replace=False
   779	                    ))
   780	                keep_indices = sorted(set(keep_indices))
   781	            else:
   782	                proxy_compressed_tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(proxy_result[0], add_special_tokens=False)
   783	                # Keep first k tokens + proxy-selected tokens
   784	                keep_indices = list(range(k)) + [k + i for i in range(len(proxy_compressed_tokens))]
   785	                keep_indices = sorted(set(keep_indices))
   786	                # If still too many, trim to rate
   787	                if len(keep_indices) > len(tokens) / rate:
   788	                    keep_indices = keep_indices[:int(len(tokens) / rate)]
   789	
   790	            kept_tokens = [tokens[i] for i in keep_indices]
   791	            compressed_text = self.tokenizer.decode(kept_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
   792	
   793	            return compressed_text, {
   794	                "sink_k": k,
   795	                "num_kept": len(keep_indices),
   796	                "original_len": len(tokens),
   797	                "compressed_len": len(keep_indices)
   798	            }
   799	        except Exception as e:
   800	            logger.error(f"Attention-Sink compression failed: {e}")

### [56] THINKING · 2026-09-20 17:14:09 UTC

```
Now I have a clear understanding of what happened in iteration 1. Let me summarize the key bugs:

1. **LLMLingua rate parameter bug**: The LLMLingua library expects a `rate` parameter in range [0, 1] (compression rate), but the code was passing compression ratios (2x, 4x, 8x). The fix: rate = 1/ratio.

2. **Calibration profile build failure**: The calibration profile failed to build (line 46 in log shows "Failed to build calibration profile"). Need to debug this.

3. **Integer conversion bug**: "Experiment failed: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer" - this is likely from the `int(n_tokens / rate)` where rate is a float (2.0, 4.0, 8.0).

4. **Dataset loading failure**: LongBench couldn't load, fell back to synthetic data.

5. **Model loading failure**: GPT-2 was used instead of LLaMA-3-8B (no GPU available in test environment, but the real run will have GPU).

6. **MINI_SPLIT_SIZE was 5** but should be 50.

Now let me also research the current LLMLingua API and attention rollout implementations to make sure I have the right approach. Let me do some web research
```

    41	- `context_budget`: str, percentage like "100%"
    42	- `rank_method`: str, "longllmlingua", "llmlingua", etc.
    43	- `use_sentence_level_filter`: bool
    44	- `context_budget_margin`: int
    45	- `target_device`: str, "cuda" or "cpu"
    46	
    47	### Return Value
    48	Dict with keys: `compressed_prompt`, `compressed_tokens`, `origin_tokens`, `ratio`, `saving`
    49	
    50	## LLMLingua-2
    51	
    52	### Package Info
    53	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua2` (or part of `llmlingua` v2+)
    54	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua (llmlingua-2 folder)
    55	- **Import**: `from llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` (v2+)
    56	
    57	### API Differences from v1
    58	- Simpler API
    59	- Uses `compression_ratio` parameter (ratio > 1, e.g., 2.0 = 50% compression)
    60	- Different model loading
    61	
    62	## LongLLMLingua
    63	
    64	### Package Info
    65	- **Package Name**: `longllmlingua` or part of `llmlingua`
    66	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LongLLMLingua
    67	- **Import**: `from longllmlingua import LongLLMLingua` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` with `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    68	
    69	### Key Parameters
    70	- Similar to LLMLingua but optimized for long contexts
    71	- Uses `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    72	
    73	## PyPI Current Versions (as of 2024-2025)
    74	- llmlingua: latest version
    75	- llmlingua2: latest version
    76	- longllmlingua: latest version
````

    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:

<hypothesis>
kind: hypothesis
title: Target-Model-Guided Prompt Compression via Attention Saliency
hypothesis: >-
  Using the target LLM's own attention-saliency maps or gradient-based input attribution (e.g., integrated gradients, attention
  rollout) to select which prompt tokens to retain will outperform proxy-model-based compression (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua,
  LLMLingua-2) because it directly captures what the target model actually uses for generation, rather than what a small proxy
  model thinks is important.
motivation: >-
  All existing prompt compression methods (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2, Selective-Context, PCRL, Perception Compressor)
  use a SMALL PROXY MODEL (GPT-2, LLaMA-7B, BERT, etc.) to estimate token importance. This creates a distribution mismatch:
  the proxy model's notion of 'important tokens' may not match what the actual target LLM attends to during generation. By
  using the target model's own attention or gradient-based saliency, we directly measure what the target model uses, eliminating
  the proxy gap. This is especially impactful for open models (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen) where we have full white-box access to
  attention maps.
assumptions:
- >-
  The target LLM's attention patterns or input gradients correlate with token importance for the downstream task
- >-
  White-box access to the target model is available (open-weight models like LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen)
- >-
  Attention-saliency can be computed efficiently (single forward pass or few backward passes) relative to the compression
  budget
- >-
  The target model's attention on the prompt tokens is stable across similar prompts/tasks (enabling caching or reuse)
investigation_approach: >-
  Implement a tiny experiment comparing three compression strategies on LongBench (single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization)
  using LLaMA-3-8B as the target model: (1) LLMLingua (GPT-2 perplexity baseline), (2) LongLLMLingua (query-aware contrastive
  perplexity), (3) Target-Model-Guided: compute attention rollout or integrated gradients from the target model on a calibration
  set, use mean attention-to-prompt or gradient magnitude per token as importance score, compress by retaining top-k tokens.
  Measure F1/ROUGE vs compression ratio. Total compute: <1 GPU-hour on a single A100/H100.
success_criteria: >-
  Target-model-guided compression achieves higher task performance (F1 for QA, ROUGE for summarization) than LLMLingua and
  LongLLMLingua at the same compression ratios (2x, 4x, 8x) on at least 2 of 3 LongBench task categories. A null result (no
  improvement) would still be informative—it would suggest the proxy models already capture the target model's token importance
  well, or that attention-saliency is not the right signal.
related_works:
- >-
  LLMLingua (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023): Uses GPT-2/LLaMA-7B perplexity as proxy for token importance. Fundamentally differs
  by using a small proxy model instead of the target model's own attention.
- >-
  LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al., ACL 2024): Adds query-awareness via contrastive perplexity (perplexity shift when conditioned
  on question). Still uses a proxy model (LLaMA-7B) for all importance estimates.
- >-
  LLMLingua-2 (Pan et al., ACL Findings 2024): Trains a BERT-based token classifier on GPT-4 distilled data. Task-agnostic,
  uses bidirectional context but still a proxy model (XLM-RoBERTa/mBERT), not the target LLM.
- >-
  Selective-Context (Li et al., 2023): Uses self-information from a small LM. Proxy-based, no query awareness.
- >-
  PCRL (Jung & Kim, 2023): RL-based discrete compression with ROUGE reward. Trains a policy on a small model (DistilBERT),
  not the target LLM.
- >-
  Perception Compressor (Tang et al., NAACL 2025): Training-free, uses guiding questions and contrast perplexity from a small
  LM. Still proxy-based.
- >-
  Attention-based KV cache compression (e.g., Keyformer, PyramidInfer): Uses target model attention to drop KV cache entries
  DURING generation, not for prompt compression BEFORE generation. Different problem setting.
inspiration: >-
  Cross-domain transfer from mechanistic interpretability (attribution patching, activation patching) and model compression
  (attention-guided pruning). In mechanistic interpretability, we routinely use the target model's own attention/activations
  to understand its behavior. In model compression (e.g., MiniLMv2, attention distillation), we use teacher model attention
  to guide student training. The novel move is applying target-model attention/attribution to PROMPT COMPRESSION (selecting
  input tokens) rather than model compression (selecting weights/heads) or KV cache compression (selecting past keys/values).
  This connects the interpretability insight 'the model tells you what it attends to' with the prompt compression problem
  'which input tokens matter'.
terms:
- term: Proxy model
  definition: >-
    A smaller, faster model (e.g., GPT-2, LLaMA-7B, BERT) used to estimate token importance for compressing prompts intended
    for a larger target LLM
- term: Target model
  definition: >-
    The actual LLM that will process the compressed prompt at inference time (e.g., LLaMA-3-8B, Mistral-7B, GPT-4)
- term: Attention rollout
  definition: >-
    A method to compute token-to-token attribution by recursively multiplying attention matrices across layers, showing how
    much each input token contributes to each output token
- term: Integrated gradients
  definition: >-
    A gradient-based attribution method that integrates gradients along a straight-line path from a baseline input to the
    actual input, providing token-level importance scores
- term: Attention-saliency map
  definition: >-
    A per-token importance score derived from the target model's attention patterns, e.g., mean attention received by each
    prompt token across heads and layers
- term: Contrastive perplexity
  definition: >-
    LongLLMLingua's metric: perplexity(token | context) - perplexity(token | question, context), measuring how much the question
    reduces uncertainty about a token
summary: >-
  Current prompt compression methods all rely on small proxy models to decide which tokens to keep. This hypothesis proposes
  using the target LLM's own attention-saliency or gradient-based input attribution directly—measuring what the target model
  actually attends to—eliminating the proxy gap. Tiny experiments on LongBench with LLaMA-3-8B can validate this in <1 GPU-hour.
alternates:
- title: Calibration-Set Attention Distillation
  hypothesis: >-
    Instead of computing attention per-query, pre-compute a universal token-importance profile for the target model on a small
    calibration set (e.g., 100 diverse prompts), then use this static profile for all future compressions. This amortizes
    the white-box cost and tests whether the target model has consistent attention patterns across tasks.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    If the target model's attention-to-prompt-tokens is relatively stable across tasks (e.g., always attends to instructions,
    entity names, question words), a one-time calibration suffices. This would be dramatically faster than per-query attribution
    and more practical for production. It beats the main hypothesis if per-query computation is the bottleneck and attention
    patterns are task-invariant.
- title: Hybrid Proxy-Target Compression
  hypothesis: >-
    Use the proxy model (e.g., LLMLingua-2) for coarse-grained document/sentence selection (cheap, fast), then apply target-model
    attention-saliency only for fine-grained token selection within the retained segments. This combines the efficiency of
    proxy models with the accuracy of target-model guidance.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    Pure target-model attribution on 10k-token prompts may be slow. Coarse proxy filtering reduces the token budget for expensive
    target-model attribution. This beats the main hypothesis if the compute budget is tight and coarse proxy decisions are
    already near-optimal, leaving only fine-grained selection to benefit from target-model signals.
- title: Gradient-Free Attention Sinks for Black-Box Target Models
  hypothesis: >-
    For API-only target models (no white-box access), use the 'attention sink' phenomenon (first few tokens accumulate disproportionate
    attention) as a proxy for the target model's internal attention: retain tokens that would become attention sinks (early
    instruction tokens, question tokens) and use a small proxy model for the rest.
  why_it_could_win: >-
    The main hypothesis requires white-box access. If the attention sink pattern is universal and predictable, we can approximate
    target-model attention without access. This beats the main hypothesis in black-box settings (OpenAI API, Anthropic API)
    where the main hypothesis is inapplicable. It wins if attention sinks reliably indicate target-model importance across
    diverse prompts.
_relation_rationale: >-
  Same conceptual frame; defects in experimental pipeline prevent any evidence from bearing on the claim.
_confidence_delta: decreased

  Run the complete wide-screen experiment on the real LongBench mini-split (450 examples, 50 per task × 9 tasks) with LLaMA-3-8B
  4-bit quantized as target model, comparing all 7 compression methods + baseline at 2x/4x/8x compression ratios. Fix all
  Iteration 1 bugs: LLMLingua rate parameter (convert ratios 2x/4x/8x → rates 0.5/0.25/0.125), calibration profile building,
  float-to-int conversion, synthetic data fallback, MINI_SPLIT_SIZE=50. Output per-example metrics (F1, ROUGE-L) AND full
  statistical analysis: bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 resamples) for all method×category×ratio cells, paired bootstrap significance
  tests (Attention Rollout vs each proxy baseline and vs Baseline), validated pre-registered rank-based selection protocol,
  corrected rank tables with real distributions.
approach: >-
  Modify the existing method.py from art_nzZ_rM-e6Rwh: (1) Load LLaMA-3-8B with 4-bit quantization (bitsandbytes) on A100/H100;
  (2) Use real LongBench mini-split from art_5_Iw7LOgL61k (processed_data/mini_data_out.json); (3) Fix LLMLingua rate parameter:
  compression_ratio → rate = 1/ratio; (4) Fix calibration profile: pre-compute attention rollout on 20 diverse calibration
  prompts from the holdout split, average per-position importance; (5) Fix integer conversion: ensure all token counts and
  indices are int; (6) Implement all 7 methods: LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2, Attention Rollout (per-query), Calibration
  Distilled, Hybrid (LLMLingua-2 coarse 2x → attention fine), Attention Sink (first-k + proxy); (7) Run full 450 × 8 × 3 =
  10,800 evaluations; (8) Compute bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance tests inline; (9) Validate ranking
  protocol: rank by (F1+ROUGE-L)/2 per (category, ratio), average across 9 cells; (10) Output method_out.json with per-example
  results AND aggregate statistics tables for direct paper inclusion.

summary: >-

  LongLLMLingua (query-aware contrastive perplexity), and Selective Context (information-theoretic token filtering). It provides
  exact implementation patterns, hyperparameter recommendations, and a runnable recipe card. It also proposes a small novel
  variant, Calibrated Attention Dropout Compression (CADC), which caches target-model attention priors to guide proxy-based
  token dropping. The output includes an evaluation protocol for LongBench with LLaMA-3-8B, compute requirements, and failure-mode
  fallbacks. Confidence is moderate for the underlying papers; exact current package APIs should be verified against official
  repositories before coding.

     1	# LLMLingua, LLMLingua-2, LongLLMLingua API Details
     2	
     3	## LLMLingua (Original)
     4	
     5	### Package Info
     6	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua`
     7	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua
     8	- **Import**: `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor`
     9	
    10	### PromptCompressor.compress_prompt() API
    11	
    12	```python
    13	compress_prompt(
    14	    prompt: Union[str, List[Dict]],
    15	    rate: float = 0.5,  # or compression_ratio?
    16	    instruction: str = "",
    17	    question: str = "",
    18	    target_token: int = -1,
    19	    condition_compare: bool = True,
    20	    condition_in_question: str = "after",
    21	    reorder_context: str = "sort",
    22	    dynamic_context_compression_ratio: float = 0.0,
    23	    context_budget: str = "100%",
    24	    rank_method: str = "longllmlingua",
    25	    use_sentence_level_filter: bool = True,
    26	    context_budget_margin: int = 5,
    27	    target_device: str = "cuda"
    28	) -> Dict[str, Any]
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Key Parameters
    32	- `rate`: float, default 0.5 - compression rate (0-1), lower = more compression
    33	- `compression_ratio`: Alternative parameter name?
    34	- `target_token`: int, target token count
    35	- `instruction`: str, instruction for compression
    36	- `question`: str, question for compression
    37	- `condition_compare`: bool, whether to use condition comparison
    38	- `condition_in_question`: str, "before" or "after"
    39	- `reorder_context`: str, "sort", "original", "reverse"
    40	- `dynamic_context_compression_ratio`: float
    41	- `context_budget`: str, percentage like "100%"
    42	- `rank_method`: str, "longllmlingua", "llmlingua", etc.
    43	- `use_sentence_level_filter`: bool
    44	- `context_budget_margin`: int
    45	- `target_device`: str, "cuda" or "cpu"
    46	
    47	### Return Value
    48	Dict with keys: `compressed_prompt`, `compressed_tokens`, `origin_tokens`, `ratio`, `saving`
    49	
    50	## LLMLingua-2
    51	
    52	### Package Info
    53	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua2` (or part of `llmlingua` v2+)
    54	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua (llmlingua-2 folder)
    55	- **Import**: `from llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` (v2+)
    56	
    57	### API Differences from v1
    58	- Simpler API
    59	- Uses `compression_ratio` parameter (ratio > 1, e.g., 2.0 = 50% compression)
    60	- Different model loading
    61	
    62	## LongLLMLingua
    63	
    64	### Package Info
    65	- **Package Name**: `longllmlingua` or part of `llmlingua`
    66	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LongLLMLingua
    67	- **Import**: `from longllmlingua import LongLLMLingua` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` with `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    68	
    69	### Key Parameters
    70	- Similar to LLMLingua but optimized for long contexts
    71	- Uses `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    72	
    73	## PyPI Current Versions (as of 2024-2025)
    74	- llmlingua: latest version
    75	- llmlingua2: latest version
    76	- longllmlingua: latest version

    13	def fetch_file_content(owner, repo, path, branch="main"):
    14	    """Fetch file content from GitHub"""
    15	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}"
    16	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    17	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)

    19	        content = response.json()
    20	        if content.get('encoding') == 'base64':
    21	            return base64.b64decode(content['content']).decode('utf-8')
    22	        return content.get('content', '')
    23	    else:
    24	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    25	    return None
    26	
    27	def fetch_repo_tree(owner, repo, branch="main"):
    28	    """Fetch repository tree"""
    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:
    33	        return response.json()
    34	    else:
    35	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    36	    return None

    38	if __name__ == "__main__":

    40	    print("Fetching LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py...")

    42	    if content:
    43	        with open("llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py", "w") as f:
    44	            f.write(content)
    45	        print("Saved to llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py")
    46	    else:
    47	        print("Failed to fetch")
    48	    
    49	    # Fetch LLMLingua-2 if separate
    50	    print("\nFetching LLMLingua repo tree...")
    51	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LLMLingua")
    52	    if tree:

    10	# GitHub API base
    11	GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com/repos"
    12	
    13	def fetch_file_content(owner, repo, path, branch="main"):
    14	    """Fetch file content from GitHub"""
    15	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}"
    16	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    17	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    18	    if response.status_code == 200:
    19	        content = response.json()
    20	        if content.get('encoding') == 'base64':
    21	            return base64.b64decode(content['content']).decode('utf-8')
    22	        return content.get('content', '')
    23	    else:
    24	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    25	    return None
    26	
    27	def fetch_repo_tree(owner, repo, branch="main"):
    28	    """Fetch repository tree"""
    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:
    33	        return response.json()
    34	    else:
    35	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    36	    return None
    37	
    38	if __name__ == "__main__":
    39	    # Fetch LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py
    40	    print("Fetching LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py...")
    41	    content = fetch_file_content("microsoft", "LLMLingua", "llmlingua/prompt_compressor.py")
    42	    if content:
    43	        with open("llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py", "w") as f:
    44	            f.write(content)
    45	        print("Saved to llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py")
    46	    else:
    47	        print("Failed to fetch")
    48	    
    49	    # Fetch LLMLingua-2 if separate
    50	    print("\nFetching LLMLingua repo tree...")
    51	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LLMLingua")
    52	    if tree:
    53	        for item in tree.get('tree', []):
    54	            if 'llmlingua-2' in item['path'].lower() or 'llmlingua2' in item['path'].lower():
    55	                print(f"Found: {item['path']}")
    56	    
    57	    # Fetch LongLLMLingua

     4	
     5	### Package Info
     6	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua`
     7	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua
     8	- **Import**: `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor`
     9	
    10	### PromptCompressor.compress_prompt() API
    11	
    12	```python
    13	compress_prompt(
    14	    prompt: Union[str, List[Dict]],
    15	    rate: float = 0.5,  # or compression_ratio?
    16	    instruction: str = "",
    17	    question: str = "",
    18	    target_token: int = -1,
    19	    condition_compare: bool = True,
    20	    condition_in_question: str = "after",
    21	    reorder_context: str = "sort",
    22	    dynamic_context_compression_ratio: float = 0.0,
    23	    context_budget: str = "100%",
    24	    rank_method: str = "longllmlingua",
    25	    use_sentence_level_filter: bool = True,
    26	    context_budget_margin: int = 5,
    27	    target_device: str = "cuda"
    28	) -> Dict[str, Any]
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Key Parameters
    32	- `rate`: float, default 0.5 - compression rate (0-1), lower = more compression
    33	- `compression_ratio`: Alternative parameter name?
    34	- `target_token`: int, target token count
    35	- `instruction`: str, instruction for compression
    36	- `question`: str, question for compression
    37	- `condition_compare`: bool, whether to use condition comparison
    38	- `condition_in_question`: str, "before" or "after"
    39	- `reorder_context`: str, "sort", "original", "reverse"
    40	- `dynamic_context_compression_ratio`: float
    41	- `context_budget`: str, percentage like "100%"
    42	- `rank_method`: str, "longllmlingua", "llmlingua", etc.
    43	- `use_sentence_level_filter`: bool
    44	- `context_budget_margin`: int
    45	- `target_device`: str, "cuda" or "cpu"
    46	
    47	### Return Value
    48	Dict with keys: `compressed_prompt`, `compressed_tokens`, `origin_tokens`, `ratio`, `saving`
    49	
    50	## LLMLingua-2
    51	
    52	### Package Info
    53	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua2` (or part of `llmlingua` v2+)
    54	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua (llmlingua-2 folder)
    55	- **Import**: `from llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` (v2+)
    56	
    57	### API Differences from v1
    58	- Simpler API
    59	- Uses `compression_ratio` parameter (ratio > 1, e.g., 2.0 = 50% compression)
    60	- Different model loading
    61	
    62	## LongLLMLingua
    63	
    64	### Package Info
    65	- **Package Name**: `longllmlingua` or part of `llmlingua`
    66	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LongLLMLingua
    67	- **Import**: `from longllmlingua import LongLLMLingua` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` with `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    68	
    69	### Key Parameters
    70	- Similar to LLMLingua but optimized for long contexts
    71	- Uses `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    72	
    73	## PyPI Current Versions (as of 2024-2025)
    74	- llmlingua: latest version
    75	- llmlingua2: latest version
    76	- longllmlingua: latest version

    10	# GitHub API base
    11	GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com/repos"
    12	
    13	def fetch_file_content(owner, repo, path, branch="main"):
    14	    """Fetch file content from GitHub"""
    15	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}"
    16	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    17	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    18	    if response.status_code == 200:
    19	        content = response.json()
    20	        if content.get('encoding') == 'base64':
    21	            return base64.b64decode(content['content']).decode('utf-8')
    22	        return content.get('content', '')
    23	    else:
    24	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    25	    return None
    26	
    27	def fetch_repo_tree(owner, repo, branch="main"):
    28	    """Fetch repository tree"""
    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:
    33	        return response.json()
    34	    else:
    35	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    36	    return None
    37	
    38	if __name__ == "__main__":
    39	    # Fetch LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py
    40	    print("Fetching LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py...")
    41	    content = fetch_file_content("microsoft", "LLMLingua", "llmlingua/prompt_compressor.py")
    42	    if content:
    43	        with open("llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py", "w") as f:
    44	            f.write(content)
    45	        print("Saved to llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py")
    46	    else:
    47	        print("Failed to fetch")
    48	    
    49	    # Fetch LLMLingua-2 if separate
    50	    print("\nFetching LLMLingua repo tree...")
    51	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LLMLingua")
    52	    if tree:
    53	        for item in tree.get('tree', []):
    54	            if 'llmlingua-2' in item['path'].lower() or 'llmlingua2' in item['path'].lower():
    55	                print(f"Found: {item['path']}")
    56	    
    57	    # Fetch LongLLMLingua

````
Based on the files I've already reviewed, I have the detailed API information for LLMLingua. Let me summarize the key findings:

## LLMLingua PromptCompressor API Details

### 1. Package Name to Import
```python
from llmlingua import PromptCompressor
```
Package: `llmlingua` (install via `pip install llmlingua`)

### 2. compress_prompt Function Signature
From the `llmlingua_api_details.md` file which contains the extracted API:

```python
compress_prompt(
    prompt: Union[str, List[Dict]],
    rate: float = 0.5,
    instruction: str = "",
    question: str = "",
    target_token: int = -1,
    condition_compare: bool = True,
    condition_in_question: str = "after",
    reorder_context: str = "sort",
    dynamic_context_compression_ratio: float = 0.0,
    context_budget: str = "100%",
    rank_method: str = "longllmlingua",
    use_sentence_level_filter: bool = True,
    context_budget_margin: int = 5,
    target_device: str = "cuda"
) -> Dict[str, Any]
```

### 3. Parameter: `rate` (not `compression_ratio`)
- The API uses **`rate`** parameter (not `compression_ratio`)
- Default: `0.5`

### 4. Parameter Range: 0-1
- `rate` expects a **float between 0 and 1**
- Lower values = more compression (e.g., 0.5 = 50% of original, 0.3 = 30% of original)
- This is a **compression rate**, not a compression ratio

### Return Value
Dictionary with keys:
- `compressed_prompt`: The compressed prompt string
- `compressed_tokens`: Number of tokens after compression
- `origin_tokens`: Number of original tokens
- `ratio`: Compression ratio achieved
- `saving`: Token savings

### Additional Notes
- For **LLMLingua-2** (separate package `llmlingua2`), the API uses `compression_ratio` parameter where values > 1 (e.g., 2.0 = 50% compression)
- For **LongLLMLingua**, use `rank_method="longllmlingua"` with the standard LLMLingua PromptCompressor
````

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""
     3	Script to fetch specific content from GitHub repositories for LLMLingua APIs.
     4	"""
     5	
     6	import requests
     7	import json
     8	import base64
     9	
    10	# GitHub API base
    11	GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com/repos"
    12	
    13	def fetch_file_content(owner, repo, path, branch="main"):
    14	    """Fetch file content from GitHub"""
    15	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}"
    16	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    17	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    18	    if response.status_code == 200:
    19	        content = response.json()
    20	        if content.get('encoding') == 'base64':
    21	            return base64.b64decode(content['content']).decode('utf-8')
    22	        return content.get('content', '')
    23	    else:
    24	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    25	    return None
    26	
    27	def fetch_repo_tree(owner, repo, branch="main"):
    28	    """Fetch repository tree"""
    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:
    33	        return response.json()
    34	    else:
    35	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    36	    return None
    37	
    38	if __name__ == "__main__":
    39	    # Fetch LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py
    40	    print("Fetching LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py...")
    41	    content = fetch_file_content("microsoft", "LLMLingua", "llmlingua/prompt_compressor.py")
    42	    if content:
    43	        with open("llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py", "w") as f:
    44	            f.write(content)
    45	        print("Saved to llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py")
    46	    else:
    47	        print("Failed to fetch")
    48	    
    49	    # Fetch LLMLingua-2 if separate
    50	    print("\nFetching LLMLingua repo tree...")
    51	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LLMLingua")
    52	    if tree:
    53	        for item in tree.get('tree', []):
    54	            if 'llmlingua-2' in item['path'].lower() or 'llmlingua2' in item['path'].lower():
    55	                print(f"Found: {item['path']}")
    56	    
    57	    # Fetch LongLLMLingua
    58	    print("\nFetching LongLLMLingua...")
    59	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LongLLMLingua")
    60	    if tree:
    61	        for item in tree.get('tree', []):
    62	            if item['path'].endswith('.py'):
    63	                print(f"Found: {item['path']}")

     6	import requests

     8	import base64
     9	
    10	# GitHub API base
    11	GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com/repos"
    12	
    13	def fetch_file_content(owner, repo, path, branch="main"):
    14	    """Fetch file content from GitHub"""
    15	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}"
    16	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    17	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    18	    if response.status_code == 200:
    19	        content = response.json()
    20	        if content.get('encoding') == 'base64':
    21	            return base64.b64decode(content['content']).decode('utf-8')
    22	        return content.get('content', '')
    23	    else:
    24	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    25	    return None
    26	
    27	def fetch_repo_tree(owner, repo, branch="main"):
    28	    """Fetch repository tree"""
    29	    url = f"{GITHUB_API}/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1"
    30	    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    31	    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    32	    if response.status_code == 200:
    33	        return response.json()
    34	    else:
    35	        print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    36	    return None
    37	
    38	if __name__ == "__main__":
    39	    # Fetch LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py
    40	    print("Fetching LLMLingua prompt_compressor.py...")
    41	    content = fetch_file_content("microsoft", "LLMLingua", "llmlingua/prompt_compressor.py")
    42	    if content:
    43	        with open("llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py", "w") as f:
    44	            f.write(content)
    45	        print("Saved to llmlingua_prompt_compressor.py")
    46	    else:
    47	        print("Failed to fetch")
    48	    
    49	    # Fetch LLMLingua-2 if separate
    50	    print("\nFetching LLMLingua repo tree...")
    51	    tree = fetch_repo_tree("microsoft", "LLMLingua")
    52	    if tree:
    53	        for item in tree.get('tree', []):
    54	            if 'llmlingua-2' in item['path'].lower() or 'llmlingua2' in item['path'].lower():
    55	                print(f"Found: {item['path']}")
    56	    
    57	    # Fetch LongLLMLingua

     3	## LLMLingua (Original)
     4	
     5	### Package Info
     6	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua`
     7	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua
     8	- **Import**: `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor`
     9	
    10	### PromptCompressor.compress_prompt() API
    11	
    12	```python
    13	compress_prompt(
    14	    prompt: Union[str, List[Dict]],
    15	    rate: float = 0.5,  # or compression_ratio?
    16	    instruction: str = "",
    17	    question: str = "",
    18	    target_token: int = -1,
    19	    condition_compare: bool = True,
    20	    condition_in_question: str = "after",
    21	    reorder_context: str = "sort",
    22	    dynamic_context_compression_ratio: float = 0.0,
    23	    context_budget: str = "100%",
    24	    rank_method: str = "longllmlingua",
    25	    use_sentence_level_filter: bool = True,
    26	    context_budget_margin: int = 5,
    27	    target_device: str = "cuda"
    28	) -> Dict[str, Any]
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Key Parameters
    32	- `rate`: float, default 0.5 - compression rate (0-1), lower = more compression
    33	- `compression_ratio`: Alternative parameter name?
    34	- `target_token`: int, target token count
    35	- `instruction`: str, instruction for compression
    36	- `question`: str, question for compression
    37	- `condition_compare`: bool, whether to use condition comparison
    38	- `condition_in_question`: str, "before" or "after"
    39	- `reorder_context`: str, "sort", "original", "reverse"
    40	- `dynamic_context_compression_ratio`: float
    41	- `context_budget`: str, percentage like "100%"
    42	- `rank_method`: str, "longllmlingua", "llmlingua", etc.
    43	- `use_sentence_level_filter`: bool
    44	- `context_budget_margin`: int
    45	- `target_device`: str, "cuda" or "cpu"
    46	
    47	### Return Value
    48	Dict with keys: `compressed_prompt`, `compressed_tokens`, `origin_tokens`, `ratio`, `saving`
    49	
    50	## LLMLingua-2
    51	
    52	### Package Info
    53	- **Package Name**: `llmlingua2` (or part of `llmlingua` v2+)
    54	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua (llmlingua-2 folder)
    55	- **Import**: `from llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` (v2+)
    56	
    57	### API Differences from v1
    58	- Simpler API
    59	- Uses `compression_ratio` parameter (ratio > 1, e.g., 2.0 = 50% compression)
    60	- Different model loading
    61	
    62	## LongLLMLingua
    63	
    64	### Package Info
    65	- **Package Name**: `longllmlingua` or part of `llmlingua`
    66	- **GitHub**: https://github.com/microsoft/LongLLMLingua
    67	- **Import**: `from longllmlingua import LongLLMLingua` or `from llmlingua import PromptCompressor` with `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    68	
    69	### Key Parameters
    70	- Similar to LLMLingua but optimized for long contexts
    71	- Uses `rank_method="longllmlingua"`
    72	
    73	## PyPI Current Versions (as of 2024-2025)
    74	- llmlingua: latest version
    75	- llmlingua2: latest version
    76	- longllmlingua: latest version

Skills are self-contained capabilities with instructions, context, and tools.

- aii-web-tools: Free-first web search (general + scholarly modes), page/PDF fetch as markdown, regex grep over page/PDF text
- aii-semscholar-bib: Batch-fetch BibTeX from Semantic Scholar
- aii-openrouter-llms: Search and call 300+ LLMs via OpenRouter
- aii-hf-datasets: Search, preview, download HuggingFace datasets
- aii-owid-datasets: Search and load Our World in Data tables

- aii-paper-to-latex: Assemble LaTeX papers and compile to PDF
- aii-parallel-computing: GPU acceleration, CPU parallelism, async I/O
- aii-python: Python coding standards for experiment scripts
- aii-use-hardware: Detect CPU/RAM/GPU, memory-safe processing
- aii-long-running-tasks: Gradual scaling pattern for long-running tasks
- aii-colab: Google Colab runtime constraints for notebooks
- aii-file-size-limit: Check and split oversized output files
</skills>

<software_constraints>
- Python only implementation

<available_tools>
Web research is available through the aii-web-tools skill, in three levels (broad → specific):

1. web search — Returns titles, URLs, snippets. Use first to discover and scan the landscape. Two modes: general (default, broad web) and scholarly (peer-reviewed papers + citations) — pass mode=scholarly for prior-art, related-work, and citation lookups.
2. web fetch — Reads a page and returns its content as markdown (HTML or PDF). Use to understand a source. May miss specific details — use fetch_grep below if it doesn't find what you need.
3. fetch_grep — Regex search over a page/PDF's full text. Returns exact matching sections with context. Use for precise details, exact numbers, methodology, or PDFs.

Workflow: search → fetch (understand) → fetch_grep (extract specifics).
</available_tools>

<tool_use>

- Search then fetch results → sequential (need URLs first)

- NEVER kill processes by name (`killall`, `pkill -f`, `ps aux | grep ... | xargs kill`). This kills OTHER runs' processes.
- NEVER monitor processes by name (`ps aux | grep method.py`). You will see other runs' processes and get confused.
- ALWAYS use PID-based process management:
  Run: `uv run method.py & PID=$!` or `timeout <seconds> uv run method.py & PID=$!`
